name: Frozen Custard With The Fruit Frozen In
description: Historical recipe from Common Sense in the Household (1871). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: eggs, and three cups of sugar beaten up with the yolks
ingredients.originalText: 6 eggs, and three cups of sugar beaten up with the yolks

ingredients.name: 1 pint fresh peaches, cut up small, or fresh ripe berries
ingredients.originalText: 1 pint fresh peaches, cut up small, or fresh ripe berries
ingredients.quantityText: 1 pint fresh peaches, cut up small, or fresh ripe berries

instructions.text: Heat the quart of milk almost to boiling, and add gradually to the beaten yolks and sugar
Whip in the frothed whites, return to the custard-kettle, and stir until it is a thick, soft custard
Let it get perfectly cold, beat in the cream and freeze
If you let it freeze itself, stir in the fruit after the second beating; if you turn the freezer, when the custard is like congealed mush

source.author: Marion Harland
source.originalInstructions:
1. Heat the quart of milk almost to boiling, and add gradually to the beaten yolks and sugar
2. Whip in the frothed whites, return to the custard-kettle, and stir until it is a thick, soft custard
3. Let it get perfectly cold, beat in the cream and freeze
4. If you let it freeze itself, stir in the fruit after the second beating; if you turn the freezer, when the custard is like congealed mush
